A run can be driven on the **codex** harness, by signing its workspace in on the `openai` provider lane: `OPENAI_API_KEY=... just minds-evals-run $DS codex-sol-low 3 --ak lane=openai --ak model=gpt-5.6-sol --ak effort=low`. The lane takes a pasted API key through the same accounts flow the other non-claude lanes use, so nothing about the run line differs beyond the lane's name, and the workspace's accounts listing reports the harness as `codex`. The key is read from `OPENAI_API_KEY` when `--ak key_env=` names none. Like the other single-provider lanes, `openai` takes no `--ak key_provider=`, and `--ak proxy=true` is still refused there: the in-box proxy meters the `anthropic` lane only.

Model ids on codex are whatever the account's catalog lists, which on an API key is the one bundled into the codex release the template pins (codex 0.154.0): `gpt-6-astra`, `gpt-5.6-sol` and `gpt-5.6-terra` with efforts `low` through `ultra`, `gpt-5.6-luna` with `low` through `max`, then `gpt-5.5` and `gpt-5.2` with efforts `low`, `medium`, `high` and `xhigh`. `--ak fast=true` selects codex's `priority` service tier, which every one of those offers except `gpt-5.2`. The observed-model confirmation now picks its naming rule by lane, because the lane is what says which harness reads the id: claude's ids are aliases resolved through a table, pi's tags report as everything after their first segment, and a codex id reports as itself. The comparison follows the lane too: a claude reported name carries a release date and so is matched by prefix, while a codex name is matched exactly -- a config asking for `gpt-5.5` is not confirmed by a chat that answered as `gpt-5.5-mini`.

**A codex trial cannot yet confirm its model or account for its spend.** mngr's codex transcript emitter writes no per-step `model_name`, so such a trial records `observed_models: []`, an empty `welcome_model` and `is_model_confirmed: null` however well the switch went; `model_choice_switch: "applied"` is all the arm's harness config then says about what it ran on, though the chat's own message feed still names the model each codex turn ran on. Neither renderer of that fact calls such a trial unconfirmed: the Slack report raises no "model unconfirmed" note on a lane that can never name a model, and `check-run`'s step-summary `arm` cell reads `openai gpt-5.6-sol not observable` rather than `unconfirmed`. So "unconfirmed" keeps meaning what it says -- a claude or pi arm whose model nothing confirmed -- rather than standing permanently against every codex cell. Its spend is unknown for a separate reason: the workspace reports no token count for a codex turn, so `usage.json` holds zero tokens and a `cost_usd` of `null` -- unknown rather than free, which is what keeps a codex arm out of a cost comparison. Read one for its conversation and its outcome scores, and never compare its cost against another arm's; the decider's and the verification agent's own figures are unaffected. Its `quality` score is not comparable either, and the README says which way it bends: the judged transcript's executing-tool scan does not know codex's spellings, so a codex trial's command output reaches neither the judged transcript nor the harness report, its progress timeline comes out empty, and an empty timeline is scored 10 by rule -- one free full mark out of the dimension's five criteria, with the gate that would catch it inert for the same reason.

The scheduled matrix runs codex nightly, as two configs in `configs/harness_configs.json`: `codex-sol-low` on `gpt-5.6-sol` at effort `low`, and `codex-terra` on `gpt-5.6-terra` at effort `medium`, both at standard speed. Both name their model rather than leaving it unset, because codex picks its default by sorting its bundled catalog and taking the first model its picker would show -- so an unset model would drift with the template's pinned codex version. Each then names the effort its own catalog entry defaults to, so each cell runs its model the way codex would by default; the two are two price points rather than a controlled comparison, since they differ in effort as well as model. A third config, `codex-astra-low`, runs `gpt-6-astra` at `low` -- the model and effort codex 0.154.0 picks for itself -- and is not nightly, so it runs only when a dispatch names it. Their cells read the workspace key from `OPENAI_API_KEY`, which the workflow fetches per cell from `mngr/ci/OPENAI_API_KEY`; a cell whose lane key is missing from Vault fails at the fetch step, before it builds a box, and leaves the other cells alone. The two nightly cells report on the **main** pair alone for now: a nightly set runs against every pair, and the `openai` lane's pasted-key sign-in is newer than the tag the `released` pair pins, so a released-pair codex cell is refused at sign-in every trial until a release carries that template -- a red column to expect there rather than to read as a regression.
